meta.notes: SINGLE-FILER FIGURES verified 2026-08-15 against S.C. Code 12-6-510(C)(1) and 12-6-1140(15) as enacted by H.4216 (scstatehouse.gov bill text) and SCDOR's H.4216 page. Brackets are NOT filing-status dependent — the $30,000 threshold is uniform across filing statuses (and is status-independent by construction: 5.21% x 30,000 - 966 = 597 = 1.99% x 30,000). SCIAD single is $15,000, reduced by (FAGI - $40,000) / $55,000 and gone at FAGI $95,000 — exactly half the MFJ parameters at both ends, but written out rather than derived. The retirement-income deduction ($3,000 / $10,000) and the 65+ deduction ($15,000) are already PER INDIVIDUAL TAXPAYER under 12-6-1170, so a one-person household simply claims one set and no single-specific values exist. TY2026 restructure: two brackets — 1.99% up to $30,000 and 5.21% above (statutory form 5.21% x TI - $966, identical). Starting point moved to FEDERAL AGI; the SC Income Adjusted Deduction (SCIAD, $30,000 MFJ) replaces the federal standard deduction and phases out proportionally over FAGI $80,000-$190,000 MFJ. Retirement-income deduction ($3,000 under 65 / $10,000 65+ per taxpayer) and the 65+ $15,000 deduction (reduced by retirement deduction claimed) were retained. Social Security is not taxed. The $30,000 bracket threshold is not indexed. From 2027 the top rate may step down on revenue triggers — not assumed.
